mainTopic: Hand-washing at a meal and מים אחרונים, then אביי's list of customs whose true reasons are health, poverty, and protection from מזיקין
overview: This amud finishes רבי ינאי's rule about hot water for washing hands. In a second version his rule applies to the final washing (מים אחרונים), and from it the גמרא infers that even scalding water is allowed for the first washing. רב נחמן teaches that the middle washing is optional, except between a cooked dish and cheese, where it is required. רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא explains that מים אחרונים are a חובה because of dangerous מלח סדומית, which can blind the eyes. Then comes a long series of אביי's teachings: 'At first I thought the reason for this custom was simple, but my teacher told me the real reason.' These cover not washing onto the ground, not taking things off the table while someone drinks, gathering crumbs, avoiding foam, eating from a tied bundle, vegetables that fell from the table, sitting under a gutter, and pouring a little water out of a pitcher. Stories support these teachings: the angel of poverty and the careful man, a witch on a boat, the demon under the gutter who had to pay for a wine barrel, and a demon-servant in רב פפא's house. That last story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the first version: very hot water may not be used
steps.stepSummary: The first version of רבי ינאי's statement ends: if the water is so hot that the hand pulls back from it, one may not wash with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: [...as long as the hand does not] recoil from it. But if the hand recoils from it, one may not wash with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that started on the previous page. In this first version, רבי ינאי allows hot water for the first washing only when it is not too hot to touch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that מים ראשונים may be hot or cold. In this first version, רבי ינאי limits that: hot is fine, but not water so hot that the hand jumps back from it. That kind of water may not be used.

keyTerms.meaning: Recoils or pulls back, as a hand does from scalding heat
The first washing of the hands, before eating bread
We wash the hands (literally, 'we take' water)

phrases.english: recoils from it,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: hot water is fine as long as the hand does not pull back from it.

phrases.english: but if the hand recoils from it
one may not wash with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בָּהֶן אֵין נוֹטְלִין בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי ינאי's statement from the previous page (first version, attached to the רישא).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מים ראשונים, hot water is allowed only if the hand does not recoil from it.

steps.title: Second version: the rule applies to the final washing
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רבי ינאי's statement on the later clause: the cold-only rule for מים אחרונים forbids only water too hot to touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this statement on the later clause: 'For final waters, one washes only with cold, not with hot.' רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי ינאי: They said this only when the hand recoils from the water. But if the hand does not recoil, one may wash with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי ינאי's statement. In this version, he is limiting the rule for the final washing, not the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that מים אחרונים must be cold. In this version, רבי ינאי says 'hot' there means only scalding water. Warm water that the hand can stand is fine even for מים אחרונים.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it (another version of the statement)
The later clause of a ברייתא or משנה
They taught this only in a certain case (a limiting phrase)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first, רבי ינאי's limit is on the first washing. In the second, it is on the final washing, so the two versions lead to different results for very hot water.

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on the latter clause:
Final waters — one washes only with cold,
but with hot — no.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yannai said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: They taught this only where the hand recoils from it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין הַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בָּהֶן – נוֹטְלִין.
phrases.english: but if the hand does not recoil from it — one may wash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the same statement of רבי ינאי from the first clause to the later clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מים אחרונים, only scalding water is forbidden; warm water the hand can bear is allowed.

steps.title: Inference: very hot water is fine for the first washing
steps.stepSummary: From the second version, the גמרא infers that for מים ראשונים even scalding water is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that for first waters, even if the hand recoils from the water, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the second version. Since רבי ינאי limited only the final washing, the first washing has no such limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, רבי ינאי placed his limit on מים אחרונים alone. So for מים ראשונים, the ברייתא's 'hot or cold' stays fully open, even for scalding water. This is the practical difference between the two versions.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; we can infer from this

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: for the first washing, water too hot to touch is not allowed. Version 2: for the final washing, only water too hot to touch is not allowed, so for the first washing even very hot water is allowed.

phrases.english: This implies that for first waters,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַיָּד סוֹלֶדֶת בָּהֶן – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: even if the hand recoils from it — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the second version for מים ראשונים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the second version, scalding water may be used for מים ראשונים.

steps.title: Middle washing is optional, but not between a cooked dish and cheese
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן limits the ברייתא's rule that the middle washing is optional: between a cooked dish and cheese, washing is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Middle waters are optional.' רב נחמן said: They taught this only between one cooked dish and another. But between a cooked dish and cheese, washing is an obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, that the middle washing is optional. רב נחמן explains that this is true only in some cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing in the middle of a meal, between dishes, is normally a choice. רב נחמן says that between a cooked dish and cheese it becomes a חובה. The סוגיא here is dealing with separating meat food from dairy.

keyTerms.meaning: Middle waters: washing during the meal, between dishes

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that an 'optional' washing can become required when meat-type food is followed by dairy.

phrases.english: Middle waters are optional.
Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֵּין תַּבְשִׁיל לְתַבְשִׁיל,
phrases.english: They taught this only between one cooked dish and another cooked dish,
but between a cooked dish and cheese — it is an obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶמְצָעִיִּים רְשׁוּת. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בֵּין תַּבְשִׁיל לְתַבְשִׁיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא (middle waters).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Middle washing is optional between two cooked dishes but required between a cooked dish and cheese.

steps.title: Why final waters are required: dangerous salt
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא explains that מים אחרונים are a חובה because of מלח סדומית, which can blind the eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רבי חייא, said: Why did they say final waters are an obligation? Because there is Sodomite salt, which blinds the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the ברייתא's line that מים אחרונים are required. רב יהודה gives the reason: a safety danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not טהרה, as with the first washing; it is a health danger. מלח סדומית may stay on the hands after eating, and if one touches his eyes it can blind him. So washing after the meal is required.

keyTerms.meaning: The final washing of the hands, after the meal
Sodomite salt, a dangerous salt from the area of סדום

steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing that the reason is danger, not טהרה, explains the next steps about how common the salt is and who must wash.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiyya, said:
For what reason did they say
that final waters are an obligation?
Because there is Sodomite salt,
which blinds the eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to explain the next line of the ברייתא (final waters).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מים אחרונים are required because of the danger of מלח סדומית.

steps.title: How rare the dangerous salt is
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that מלח סדומית is found only as a tiny pinch in a huge amount of salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And it is found like a pinch in a כור of salt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a detail to רב יהודה's reason: the dangerous salt is very rare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the danger is rare, a tiny pinch mixed into a huge amount, חז"ל still required washing. Because the risk is blindness, even a small chance is taken seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: A כור, a very large measure

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And it is found like a pinch in a kor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to רב יהודה's reason about how common the dangerous salt is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלח סדומית appears only rarely, about a pinch in a כור, yet the obligation still stands.

steps.title: What about someone who measured salt?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי whether someone who measured out salt must wash his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: One who measured salt, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about a case outside of eating: a person who handled salt by measuring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the reason is the dangerous salt, the question is whether this applies even without a meal. Someone who measured salt had his hands in salt, so does he need to wash?

keyTerms.meaning: One who measured salt (כָּל comes from the word for measuring)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
One who measured salt — what is the law?
phrases.notes: כָּל here means 'measured,' not 'all.' He is asking about someone who measured out salt with his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the salt reason to a new case outside of a meal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must one who measured salt wash his hands, given the danger of מלח סדומית?

steps.title: Certainly he must wash
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that this does not even need to be asked; he certainly must wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not even a question.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: of course the person who measured salt must wash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person must wash after a meal because of a little salt in the food, then someone whose hands were fully in salt surely must. The case is even more obvious than the case of a meal.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not even a question; it is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: מים אחרונים are a חובה because of the danger of מלח סדומית. Even though the salt is rare, anyone who handled salt, such as by measuring it, surely must wash.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not necessary to ask.
phrases.notes: He means: obviously he must wash, even more than someone who just ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One who measured salt certainly must wash his hands; it is obvious.

steps.title: Why final washing water is not poured on the ground
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought the reason was messiness. His teacher told him it is because a רוח רעה rests on the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I thought we do not wash with מים אחרונים onto the ground because it is dirty. My teacher told me it is because an evil spirit rests on that water.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells us how he first understood a practice about מים אחרונים, and how his teacher corrected him with a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practice stays the same: do not let the final washing water fall on the ground. Only the reason changes, from a cleanliness concern (זוהמא) to a danger concern (רוח רעה). A danger reason is stronger, because it applies even where no one would mind the mess.

keyTerms.meaning: At first I used to say (a formula for a view the speaker later changed)
Final water, the same as מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים, the washing after the meal
An evil spirit, a harmful force

phrases.english: Abaye said: At first I used to say,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי דְּלָא מָשׁוּ מַיָּא בָּתְרָאֵי עַל אַרְעָא –
phrases.english: this, that people do not wash with final water onto the ground,
is because of messiness.
The Master said to me:
phrases.notes: "The Master" is how אביי refers to his teacher and uncle, רבה.

phrases.english: It is because an evil spirit rests upon them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of מים אחרונים from steps 5-8 by adding a related practice and its reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not wash with מים אחרונים onto the ground, because a רוח רעה rests on that water.

steps.title: Why nothing is taken off the table while someone drinks
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought the reason was that a mishap might happen at the meal. His teacher said it is because it causes רוח צרדא, a headache-spirit.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי also said: At first I thought the reason we do not take anything off the table while a person holds a cup to drink is that something might go wrong at the meal. My teacher told me it is because it is harmful and brings on a headache-spirit.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second example of a reason he once held and his teacher corrected, this time about taking items off the table while someone is drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the practice stays the same and only the reason changes. אביי thought the worry was a social or practical mishap at the meal. רבה explained it as a health danger, רוח צרדא.

keyTerms.meaning: A harmful spirit that causes headache pain

phrases.english: And Abaye said: At first I used to say,
this, that one does not take anything from the table
when a person is holding a cup to drink,
is because a mishap might happen at the meal.
The Master said to me:
It is because it is harmful, bringing a spirit of head pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement by אביי in the same pattern: his first reason, then his teacher's correction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not take items off the table while someone holds a cup to drink, because it causes רוח צרדא.

steps.title: Three limits on the table rule
steps.stepSummary: The rule against taking things off the table applies only if the item is not returned, is moved more than four אמות away, and is needed for the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: We said this only if someone takes the item and does not put it back. Taking it and putting it back is no problem. We said it only if the item is moved beyond four אמות. Within four אמות is no problem. We said it only about something needed for the meal. Something not needed for the meal is no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule from step 10, listing three conditions that must all be present for the concern to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each line uses the pattern 'we said it only when... but in this other case, there is no problem.' The concern applies only when a needed item truly leaves the table area: it is not returned and it goes past four אמות. If any one condition is missing, the worry falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: We said this only when... (a formula that limits a rule)
We have no problem with it
Four cubits, a set distance in halacha

steps.whatToRemember: The table rule applies only when a needed item is taken, not returned, and moved beyond four אמות.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא דְּשָׁקֵיל וְלָא מַהְדַּר,
phrases.english: And we said this only where one takes and does not put back,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִשְׁקַל וְאַהְדּוֹרֵי – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but taking and putting back, we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא חוּץ לְאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: And we said this only beyond four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תּוֹךְ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but within four cubits, we have no problem with it.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא מִידֵּי דִּצְרִיךְ לִסְעוֹדְתָּא,
phrases.english: And we said this only about something needed for the meal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִידֵּי דְּלָא צְרִיךְ לִסְעוֹדְתָּא – לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
phrases.english: but something not needed for the meal, we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא דְּשָׁקֵיל וְלָא מַהְדַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule stated in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern applies only to a meal-related item that is taken, not returned, and moved beyond four אמות.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי was strict even with spice tools
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי was careful not to remove even the mortar and pestle for spices while someone was drinking, since they count as items needed for the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי was careful about this even with the mortar and pestle used for spices, because they are things needed for the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how one sage applied the rule from steps 10-11 in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mortar and pestle are tools, not food, so one might think they are not 'needed for the meal.' מר בר רב אשי treated them as meal items because they are used to prepare the food's spices, so he would not remove them either.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi was particular
even about a mortar and pestle for spices,
phrases.notes: He means he would not take these off the table while someone was holding a cup to drink.

phrases.english: since they are things needed for the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי קָפֵיד אֲפִילּוּ אַאֲסִיתָא וּבוּכְנָא דְּתַבְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the third limit of step 11 (items needed for the meal) and shows how widely it reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even spice-grinding tools count as needed for the meal, so they too are not removed while someone drinks.

steps.title: Gathering crumbs protects against poverty
steps.stepSummary: אביי thought people gathered crumbs to keep things clean. His teacher told him it is because leaving crumbs brings עניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I thought people gather bread crumbs to keep things clean. But my teacher told me it is because leaving crumbs causes poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives another 'I used to think, but my teacher told me' teaching, this time about crumbs left after a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The custom stays the same, but its reason changes. אביי thought it was about neatness. His teacher said it is a matter of protecting against עניות, so the custom matters more than it looks.

keyTerms.meaning: At first I used to say (I used to think)

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
At first I used to say
that this, that people gather up the crumbs,
is because of cleanliness.
The Master told me:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' is אביי's teacher, the same one from the steps before.

phrases.english: It is because it is bad for poverty.
phrases.notes: He means that leaving crumbs around can bring poverty on a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in אביי's list of reasons he learned from his teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People gather crumbs after a meal because leaving them brings עניות, not only for cleanliness.

steps.title: The story of the man the angel of poverty could not catch
steps.stepSummary: The שרא דעניותא chased a man who was very careful with crumbs. Even when crumbs fell into grass, the man pulled up the grass and threw it in the river, and the angel had to give up.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man whom the angel of poverty kept chasing, but it could not get him, because he was very careful with crumbs. One day he ate bread over the grass. The angel said, 'Now he will surely fall into my hands.' After eating, the man brought a hoe, pulled up the grass, and threw it into the river. He heard the angel say, 'Woe! That man has driven me out of my home.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the teaching from step 13 at work: being careful with crumbs keeps poverty away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crumbs falling into grass seemed impossible to gather, so the angel thought it had finally won. The man went all the way, pulling up the grass itself. This shows how far a person should go to keep this habit.

keyTerms.meaning: The angel (spiritual force) in charge of poverty

phrases.english: There was a certain man
whom the angel of poverty kept chasing,
but it could not overpower him,
because he was very careful about crumbs.
One day he ate his bread over grass,
The angel said: Now he will surely fall into my hands.
After he ate, he brought a hoe,
pulled up the grass, and threw it into the river.
He heard it saying:
Woe, that man has driven me out of my home!
phrases.notes: Literally 'driven him out of his house.' The angel is talking about itself in a roundabout way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה מְהַדַּר עֲלֵיהּ שָׂרָא דְּעַנְיוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that shows the crumbs teaching from step 13 is true.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being careful with crumbs, even to an extreme, keeps the force of עניות away.

steps.title: Not drinking the foam prevents illness
steps.stepSummary: אביי thought people avoid the foam on a drink because it is disgusting. His teacher told him it is because it causes כרסם.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: At first I thought people don't drink the foam on a drink because it is disgusting. But my teacher told me it is because it is bad for כרסם, a kind of illness.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives one more 'I used to think, but my teacher told me' teaching, this time about the foam on top of a drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the habit stays the same, but the reason changes. It is not about taste or feeling grossed out. It is about health.

keyTerms.meaning: Foam on top of a drink
An illness (often explained as a kind of catarrh or head cold)

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
At first I used to say
that this, that people do not drink the foam,
is because it is disgusting.
The Master told me:
It is because it is bad for catarrh.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא, הַאי דְּלָא שָׁתֵי אוּפְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the same list of אביי's corrected reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking the foam is avoided because it causes כרסם.

steps.title: Every simple way of getting rid of foam causes harm
steps.stepSummary: Drinking the foam causes כרסם, blowing it off hurts the head, and pushing it away by hand brings עניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Drinking it is bad for catarrh. Blowing on it is bad for the head. Pushing it away is bad for poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that all three obvious ways of dealing with foam cause some harm. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each option brings a different kind of damage: illness, a headache, or עניות. That leaves the reader wondering what a person is supposed to do.

phrases.english: Drinking it is bad for catarrh;
blowing on it is bad for the head;
pushing it away is bad for poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands step 15 by listing the harm from each way of handling foam.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking, blowing, and pushing away the foam are each harmful.

steps.title: So what should a person do with the foam?
steps.stepSummary: Since every option is harmful, the גמרא asks what the solution is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the fix for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple practical question. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question comes straight from step 16. If drinking, blowing, and pushing away all cause harm, there must be another way.

phrases.english: What is its remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a solution after step 16 ruled out every obvious option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a person deal with foam without being harmed?

steps.title: Sink the foam into the drink
steps.stepSummary: The answer: push the foam down into the drink, then drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should sink it down into the drink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: press the foam down so it sinks into the drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sinking is a fourth option that avoids all three harms. The foam is not drunk as foam, not blown, and not pushed out of the cup.

phrases.english: He should sink it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sink the foam into the drink.

steps.title: Cures for illness from foam
steps.stepSummary: Illness from wine foam is cured with beer. Illness from beer foam is cured with water. Illness from water foam has no cure.
steps.simpleTranslation: For catarrh from wine foam, the cure is beer. For catarrh from beer foam, the cure is water. For catarrh from water foam, there is no cure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists a cure for each kind of foam illness, one drink at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each drink's illness is cured by a simpler, cheaper drink. Water is the simplest of all, so nothing is left below it to cure it.

phrases.english: For catarrh from wine, beer;
for that from beer, water;
for that from water, there is no remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds information about curing the כרסם mentioned in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Foam illness from wine is cured by beer and from beer by water; from water it has no cure.

steps.title: Poverty follows the poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ties step 19 to a well-known saying: poverty follows the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what people say: Poverty follows the poor man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up with a popular saying that fits what it just taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor person can usually afford only water. Yet sickness from water foam is exactly the one with no cure, so the poor person suffers again. That is just what the saying describes.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a popular saying)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי learned two more real reasons from his teacher. Gathering crumbs protects against עניות, and avoiding foam protects against כרסם. The right way to handle foam is to sink it into the drink.

phrases.english: And this is what people say:
Poverty follows the poor man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up step 19 with a popular saying.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The poor, who drink only water, are left without a cure, just as the saying 'poverty follows the poor' describes.

steps.title: Vegetables from a tied bundle: witchcraft, not gluttony
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought people avoid eating vegetables straight from a gardener's tied bundle because it looks greedy. His teacher told him it is because it makes a person vulnerable to כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I used to think people don't eat vegetables from a bundle the gardener tied because it looks like gluttony. My teacher told me it's because it's harmful regarding witchcraft.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shares a practice and corrects his own earlier reason for it. The real reason is protection from כשפים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practice itself stays the same. Only the reason changes. אביי thought it was about manners (looking greedy), but מר tells him it is about danger (witchcraft). This sets up the story that follows, which shows this practice really does protect.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: At first I would say,
this, that people do not eat vegetables
from a bundle that the gardener tied,
is because it looks like gluttony.
The Master said to me:
phrases.notes: "The Master" is how אביי refers to his teacher.

phrases.english: It is because it is harmful regarding witchcraft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same series of אביי's 'at first I would say… the Master told me' statements, after the side discussion of foam remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid eating vegetables straight from a gardener's tied bundle, because doing so exposes one to כשפים.

steps.title: The witch who could not harm the sages
steps.stepSummary: A woman who practiced witchcraft could not harm רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא. She explained that they avoid three practices, including eating vegetables from a tied bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא were on a boat. A certain matron asked to sit with them, and they refused. She cast a spell and tied the boat in place. They said something and freed it. She said: What can I do to you? You don't wipe with a shard, you don't kill lice on your clothes, and you don't eat vegetables from a gardener's tied bundle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that supports the reason from step 21. The witch herself admits that avoiding the tied bundle protects them from her magic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 claimed that eating from a tied bundle makes a person vulnerable to כשפים. Here a witch confirms it from her own side: she cannot harm people who avoid that practice. She also names two more protective habits.

keyTerms.meaning: A matron, a noblewoman (here, one practicing witchcraft)

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
were traveling on a boat.
A certain matron said to them:
Seat me with you. They did not seat her.
She said something and tied up the boat.
phrases.notes: "Something" means a spell, and "tied up" means the boat got stuck and couldn't move.

phrases.english: They said something and released it.
She said to them: What can I do to you,
since you do not wipe yourselves with a clay shard,
and you do not kill a louse on your garments,
and you do not eat vegetables
from a bundle that the gardener tied.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאַרְבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reason that מר gave in step 21 with a story.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that eating from a tied bundle makes one vulnerable to כשפים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The witch's own admission that she could not harm sages who avoid this practice.

steps.title: Vegetables that fell from the table: bad breath, not disgust
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought people don't eat vegetables that fell from the table because it is disgusting. מר told him it is because it causes bad breath.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I used to think people don't eat vegetables that fell from the table because it's disgusting. My teacher told me it's because it's harmful for bad breath.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second practice in the same pattern and again corrects his earlier reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like step 21, the practice stays the same but the reason changes. It moves from a matter of taste (it's gross) to a health concern (it causes bad breath).

phrases.english: And Abaye said: At first I would say,
this, that people do not eat vegetables
that fell (on the table) [from the table],
phrases.notes: Some versions say "on the table," in round brackets. The corrected wording, in square brackets, is "from the table."

phrases.english: is because of disgust.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי מָר: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָשֶׁה לְרֵיחַ הַפֶּה.
phrases.english: The Master said to me: It is because it is harmful for bad breath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second item in אביי's list of corrected reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid eating vegetables that fell from the table, because they cause bad breath.

steps.title: Not sitting under a gutter: demons, not dirty water
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought people avoid sitting under a gutter because of the waste water that pours down. מר told him it is because מזיקין are found there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I used to think people don't sit under a gutter because of the waste water poured out. My teacher told me it's because demons are commonly found there.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a third practice in the same pattern. This time the real reason is that demons are found under gutters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, a simple, practical reason (getting splashed with dirty water) is replaced with a hidden danger (מזיקין). This sets up the story in the next step, which shows a demon living under a gutter.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: At first I would say,
this, that people do not sit under a gutter,
is because of waste water.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לִי מָר: מִשּׁוּם דִּשְׁכִיחִי מַזִּיקִין.
phrases.english: The Master said to me: It is because demons are commonly found there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third item in אביי's list of corrected reasons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid sitting under a gutter, because מזיקין are commonly found there.

steps.title: The wine barrel that burst under a gutter
steps.stepSummary: Porters set a wine barrel down under a gutter and it burst. מר בר רב אשי blew shofars and placed the demon there in שמתא (excommunication).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some porters were carrying a barrel of wine. When they wanted to rest, they set it under a gutter, and it burst. They came to מר בר רב אשי, who brought out שופרות and excommunicated the demon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing that demons really are found under gutters, as מר said in step 24. This step also sets up the conversation with the demon in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barrel bursting for no clear reason, right under a gutter, shows a demon at work there. מר בר רב אשי treats the demon as a responsible party and puts it in שמתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He excommunicated it (placed it in שמתא)

phrases.english: There were certain porters
who were carrying a barrel of wine.
They wanted to rest,
so they placed it under a gutter, and it burst.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: They came before Mar bar Rav Ashi.
He brought out shofars and excommunicated it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the demon living under that gutter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ שָׁקוֹלָאֵי דַּהֲווֹ דָּרוּ חָבִיתָא דְּחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 24 with a story about a demon under a gutter.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that מזיקין are commonly found under gutters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the barrel that burst under a gutter, and the demon who answered for it.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי asks the demon why it did this
steps.stepSummary: The demon comes before מר בר רב אשי, and he asks it why it broke the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: The demon came before him. He said to it: Why did you do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The demon appears, and מר בר רב אשי demands an explanation. This question sets up the demon's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon showing up after the שמתא confirms that a demon really was there. The question invites it to explain itself.

phrases.english: It came before him.
phrases.notes: "It" is the demon, coming before מר בר רב אשי.

phrases.english: He said to it: Why did you do this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי תַּעֲבֵיד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the demon, now in שמתא, is questioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the demon broke the porters' barrel.

steps.title: The demon: they put it on my ear
steps.stepSummary: The demon answers that it had no choice, because the porters put the barrel right on its ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to him: What else should I do, when they put it on my ear?
steps.whatsHappening: The demon defends itself: the porters put the barrel right on top of it. This confirms that demons live under gutters, and the next step shows מר בר רב אשי rejecting the excuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon's answer shows that the danger comes from disturbing the demon in its spot under the gutter. That is exactly why מר taught in step 24 not to sit under a gutter.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's three corrections: not eating from a tied bundle protects against witchcraft, not eating vegetables that fell from the table prevents bad breath, and not sitting under a gutter avoids demons. Each of the two stories backs up one of these reasons.

phrases.english: It said to him: How else should I act,
when they placed it on my ear?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֵיכִי אֶעֱבֵיד, כִּי אוֹתְבֵיהּ בְּאוּנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The demon broke the barrel because the porters set it down on its ear, right where it lives under the gutter.

steps.title: The demon's excuse is rejected: you were in a public place, so pay
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי tells the demon it had no business being in a busy public place, so it is the one at fault and must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to it: What are you doing in a place where many people are found? You are the one who acted out of the ordinary. Go pay!
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי answers the demon's excuse from the last step and turns it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon said the porters put the barrel on its ear, so it was not to blame. מר בר רב אשי turns this around. A busy public place is normal for people to use, so the one who sits somewhere unusual (the demon) is the one at fault. That is why it has to pay for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: where many people are commonly found (a public place)
you deviated, acted out of the norm

phrases.english: He said to it:
phrases.notes: מר בר רב אשי is speaking to the demon.

phrases.aramaic: אַתְּ בְּדוּכְתָּא דִּשְׁכִיחִי רַבִּים מַאי בָּעֵית?
phrases.english: What are you doing in a place where many people are found?
You are the one who deviated,
go pay!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ בְּדוּכְתָּא דִּשְׁכִיחִי רַבִּים מַאי בָּעֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the demon's defense from step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The demon's claim that it was not at fault
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The demon was the one in an unusual spot in a public place, so it carries the blame.

steps.title: The demon asks for a payment date
steps.stepSummary: The demon accepts that it must pay and asks for a set time to do so. מר בר רב אשי gives it a date.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to him: Now then, let the Master set a time for me, and I will pay. He set a time for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The demon agrees to pay but asks for time, and it gets a deadline. This sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon no longer argues. It only asks for a payment date. The deadline it gets matters for the next step, when it comes late.

phrases.english: It said to him: Now then,
let the Master set a time for me, and I will pay.
He set a time for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי לִיקְבַּע לִי מָר זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The demon gives in to the ruling of step 28 and asks for time to pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A payment deadline is set for the demon.

steps.title: The demon is late: why didn't you come on time?
steps.stepSummary: The deadline passes, the demon comes late, and מר בר רב אשי asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the time arrived, it delayed. When it came, he said to it: Why did you not come at your set time?
steps.whatsHappening: The demon misses its deadline, and מר בר רב אשי asks it why. This sets up the demon's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question, not an attack. The answer in the next step tells us something new about how demons are able to get money.

keyTerms.meaning: it was delayed, it came late

phrases.english: When the time arrived, it delayed.
When it came, he said to it:
Why did you not come at your time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the deadline set in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the demon did not pay by the deadline

steps.title: Demons may only take ownerless things
steps.stepSummary: The demon explains that demons cannot take anything that is tied, sealed, measured, or counted. They can only take ownerless things, and finding those takes time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to him: Anything that is tied up, sealed, measured, or counted, we have no permission to take from it, until we find something ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The demon answers the question: it was late because it could only collect money from ownerless things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demon explains a limit on what demons are allowed to take. Anything tied, sealed, measured, or counted is off-limits. Only הפקר is allowed, so collecting the money took longer than planned.
steps.whatToRemember: The demon's story ends here. Demons are bound by rules: they can be held responsible for damage, and they may only take ownerless things.

phrases.english: It said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִילֵּי דִּצְיִיר וַחֲתִים וּכְיִיל וּמְנֵי,
phrases.english: Any item that is tied up, sealed, measured, or counted,
we have no permission to take from it,
until we find something ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל מִילֵּי דִּצְיִיר וַחֲתִים וּכְיִיל וּמְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Demons may only take ownerless property, so gathering the payment took longer.

steps.title: Pouring water from a pitcher is because of bad waters
steps.stepSummary: אביי first thought people pour a little water out of a pitcher to get rid of twigs. His teacher told him it is because of מים הרעים, harmful water.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: At first I would say that the practice of pouring out water from the mouth of a pitcher is because of twigs. The Master told me: It is because there are harmful waters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to אביי's list of customs he first misunderstood and adds a new one: pouring out a little water before drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as steps 23 and 24. אביי had a simple, practical reason (twigs). His teacher gave a deeper reason: the top of the water may hold harmful 'bad waters', so you pour some out first.

keyTerms.meaning: bad or harmful waters (a spiritual danger)

phrases.english: And Abaye said: At first I would say,
this practice of pouring water from the mouth of a pitcher —
is because of twigs.
The Master said to me:
It is because there are bad waters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to אביי's series of customs (steps 23 and 24) after the demon story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pour some water out of a pitcher before drinking because of מים הרעים.

steps.title: A demon-servant in רב פפא's house comes back late from the river
steps.stepSummary: A demon who served in רב פפא's house went to bring water from the river and came back late. The household asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain son of a demon in רב פפא's house. It went to bring water from the river, and it was delayed. When it came, they said to it: Why were you delayed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story to show that מים הרעים really exist. This step sets up the demon's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the teacher's statement in step 32. Here it only sets the scene: a demon was sent for water and came back late. The proof comes in its answer.

keyTerms.meaning: son of a demon, a young demon

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא בַּר שֵׁידָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: There was a certain son of a demon that was in Rav Pappa's house;
it went to bring water from the river, and it delayed.
When it came, they said to it:
Why did you delay?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא בַּר שֵׁידָא דַּהֲוָה בֵּי רַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story supporting the idea of מים הרעים from step 32.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the demon-servant in רב פפא's house

steps.title: The demon waited for the bad waters to pass
steps.stepSummary: The demon explains it waited until the מים הרעים flowed past before drawing water. The story then continues.
steps.simpleTranslation: It said to them: I waited until the bad waters passed. In the meantime...
steps.whatsHappening: The demon answers that it was late because it waited for the harmful waters to pass. The last word starts a new part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A demon, who would know about such things, confirms that מים הרעים really flow in rivers. That supports step 32. The word אדהכי ('in the meantime') shows the story is not over.
steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of a sentence. 'In the meantime' leads into what happens next, which comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: It said to them:
Until the bad waters passed.
In the meantime...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the household's question from step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It waited for the מים הרעים to pass before drawing water.
